## `Divider`

struct in `choscorui::prelude::Divider`

```rust
pub struct Divider;
```

A thin line across a stack: horizontal in a vertical stack, vertical
in a horizontal one. A horizontal line makes its stack take the width
offered; a vertical line spans the height of its row, but does not

## `Dock`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::Dock`

```rust
pub type Dock = Configured<DockLayout>;
```

Dockable panels around a center area, as `layout` arranges them.
Activating a tab reports the panel id through `.on_item`, and closing
a panel runs `.on_dismiss`. `.arrangement` keeps the saved text of the
arrangement in a binding. A hosted dock paints the text of each panel
and of the center: give them with `DockPanel::with_text` and
`DockLayout::with_center_text`.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Editor;

impl View for Editor {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let saved = cx.state(String::new());
        Dock::new(|_: &Env| {
            let mut dock = DockLayout::new(28.0).with_center_text("Editor");
            let files = DockPanel::new("files", "Files").with_text("12 files");
            let target = DockTarget::Tab { area: DockArea::Left, group: 0 };
            let _ = dock.add(PanelId(1), files, target);
            dock
        })
        .arrangement(saved.binding())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `Dock::arrangement`

```rust
pub fn arrangement(self, saved: Binding<String>) -> Self
```

Keeps the arrangement in `saved`, as the text of
`DockLayout::save`. Each change that the user makes in the dock
writes the text. New text restores its arrangement in the dock;
text that does not restore keeps the arrangement that the dock has.

#### `Dock::new`

```rust
pub fn new(layout: impl Fn(&Env) -> DockLayout + 'static) -> Self
```

A dock with the layout that `layout` makes.

## `Field`

struct in `choscorui::prelude::Field`

```rust
pub struct Field<C> { /* private fields */ }
```

One form field: a label, a control, and an optional description and
error. A `Vertical` field, the default, stacks them. A `Horizontal`
field puts the label at the leading edge and stacks the others beside
it. A `Responsive` field is horizontal when it gets the breakpoint
width of the `Field` layout or more, and vertical when narrower. The
gaps come from the `Field` recipe, and side-by-side parts mirror in
right-to-left layouts.

The control gets a `LabelledBy` relation to the label and a
`DescribedBy` relation to the description. While the error shows, the
control also gets a `DescribedBy` relation to the error, and its
accessibility description gives the error and then the description.
While the error shows, the control and the label are invalid: a field
control shows its invalid look, and the label uses the destructive
color. A press on the label focuses the control, and toggles a
checkbox or a switch.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Signup;

impl View for Signup {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let email = cx.state(String::new());
        Field::new("Email", TextField::new("Email", email.binding()))
            .description("We send the receipt here.")
            .error("Enter an email address.", move || email.get().is_empty())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods


```rust
            FormRow::new("Public", Switch::new("Public", public.binding())),
```

## `LazyVStack`

struct in `choscorui::prelude::LazyVStack`

```rust
pub struct LazyVStack { /* private fields */ }
```

Items top to bottom, mounted only while they show in the enclosing
scroll view or the window. Every item is `item_extent` high:
`LazyVStack::new(move || rows.get(), 32.0, |index| Text::new(format!("Row {index}")))`.

An item that scrolls out of view unmounts, and its state ends; an
item that scrolls in mounts again. The item view runs when the item
mounts, so data that changes belongs in live properties.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Log;

impl View for Log {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let rows = cx.state(10_000_usize);
        ScrollView::new(
            LazyVStack::new(move || rows.get(), 32.0, |index| {
                Text::new(format!("Row {index}"))
            })
            .spacing(Space::S1),
        )
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods


## `Resizable`

struct in `choscorui::prelude::Resizable`

```rust
pub struct Resizable<P> { /* private fields */ }
```

Panes with a handle between each two neighbors. Each top-level view of
`panes` is one pane, in order. `sizes` holds the size of each pane but
the last, which takes the rest, along the split. A drag or a key moves
one handle, changes only the two panes beside it, and writes `sizes`.
The keys, the actions, the semantics, and the look are those of the
hosted `Resizable` panel group. With
three or more panes, each handle is its own node and focus stop, with
its own slider semantics, in a group node. A horizontal group mirrors
in right-to-left layouts. The group takes the space it is offered.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Split;

impl View for Split {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let sizes = cx.state(vec![240.0]);
        let panes = (Text::new("Sidebar"), Text::new("Content"));
        Resizable::new("Panes", SplitOrientation::Horizontal, panes, sizes.binding())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `Resizable::grip`


Shows a grip on each handle.

```rust

```

## `ScrollView`

struct in `choscorui::prelude::ScrollView`

```rust
pub struct ScrollView<C> { /* private fields */ }
```

Content that scrolls along one axis. The wheel and the scroll bar
scroll it, and moving focus to a control out of view scrolls that
control into view. The scroll bar takes its look from the
`ScrollArea` recipe. With `.focusable(true)`, the scroll view takes
focus, and the arrow, page, Home, and End keys scroll it.

#### Examples

```rust
let view = ScrollView::new(VStack::new(
    (0..100).map(|row| Text::new(format!("Row {row}"))).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
));
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `ScrollView::axis`

```rust
pub fn axis(self, axis: Axis) -> Self
```

Content that scrolls along `axis`.

#### `ScrollView::new`

```rust
pub fn new(content: C) -> Self
```

Vertically scrolling content.

enum in `choscorui::prelude::VerticalAlignment`

```rust
pub enum VerticalAlignment {
    Top,

    Bottom,
    FirstBaseline,
    Fill,
}
```

Where children sit across a horizontal stack.

### Variants

- `Top`
- `Center`
- `Bottom`
- `FirstBaseline`: The first text baselines line up.
- `Fill`: Each child takes the full height.
